subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In OCR GCSE Music (J536), the solo performance is assessed as part of which component?
options: Component 01: Listening and Appraising
Component 03: Integrated Portfolio
Component 04: Practical Component
Component 02: Set Works
questions.explain: The solo performance forms one half of Component 03, the Integrated Portfolio.

questions.q: The Integrated Portfolio brings together which two musical activities?
options: Performing and composing
Listening and appraising
Composing and appraising
Performing and listening
questions.explain: The portfolio integrates a solo performance with a composition into a single body of work.

questions.q: What proportion of the total GCSE marks is the Integrated Portfolio worth?
questions.explain: The Integrated Portfolio (Component 03) is worth 30% of the total GCSE.

questions.q: The performance element of the Integrated Portfolio must take which form?
options: A solo performance
An ensemble performance
A conducted orchestral performance
A group improvisation
questions.explain: Component 03 requires a solo performance; the ensemble performance belongs to Component 04.

questions.q: In the Integrated Portfolio, the composition must be written to which kind of brief?
options: A brief set by the learner themselves
A brief set by OCR
A brief set by the exam invigilator
A prescribed set song
questions.explain: In Component 03 the learner devises their own brief for the composition.

questions.q: How does the Component 03 composition differ from the composition in Component 04?
options: Component 03 is to the learner's own brief, while Component 04 is to a brief set by OCR
Component 03 is to an OCR brief, while Component 04 is to the learner's own brief
Both compositions are written to the same OCR brief
Component 03 has no composition, only performance
questions.explain: The own-brief composition sits in the Integrated Portfolio, whereas the set-brief composition sits in the Practical Component.

questions.q: On what may a candidate perform their solo for the Integrated Portfolio?
options: Any instrument or voice, including music technology
Only orchestral instruments
Only the piano or voice
Only instruments taught at the centre
questions.explain: Learners may perform on any instrument, voice or through music technology.

questions.q: A learner plays a flute piece accompanied by a piano backing. How is this best classified?
options: A solo performance
An ensemble performance
An improvisation
A composition
questions.explain: An accompanied single performer is still a soloist, so it counts as a solo performance.

questions.q: Why is Component 03 described as an 'Integrated Portfolio'?
options: It draws together a learner's performing and composing into one portfolio
It integrates several different exam boards' requirements
It is completed under integrated exam conditions in one sitting
It combines listening, performing and composing in a written paper
questions.explain: The performance and composition are collected as an integrated portfolio of practical work.

questions.q: How is the Integrated Portfolio assessed?
options: Marked by the centre and moderated by OCR as non-examined assessment
Sat as a written examination marked by OCR
Marked entirely by OCR examiners in a live exam
Assessed by an external visiting examiner on the day
questions.explain: As non-examined assessment, the centre marks the work and OCR moderates it.

questions.q: A learner sets themselves the brief: 'Compose a minimalist piece for string quartet.' In which component does this composition belong?
options: Component 03: Integrated Portfolio
Component 04: Practical Component
Component 01: Listening and Appraising
It is not permitted in any component
questions.explain: A composition written to the learner's own brief belongs in the Integrated Portfolio.

questions.q: What key freedom does writing to one's own brief give the learner?
options: Choosing the style, structure and stimulus of the composition
Choosing which exam board will mark the work
Deciding the overall weighting of the component
Selecting which set works are studied
questions.explain: The own brief lets the learner determine the starting point and creative direction of the piece.

questions.q: Across both non-examined components (03 and 04), the total performing time must be at least how long?
options: Four minutes
One minute
Ten minutes
Twenty minutes
questions.explain: OCR requires a combined minimum of four minutes of performing across the two practical components.

questions.q: Tom wants to submit a duet in which two players share the melody equally as his Integrated Portfolio performance. Why is this unsuitable?
options: Component 03 requires a solo performance, not an ensemble
Duets are banned across the whole qualification
The piece would automatically be too short
Duets can only be composed, not performed
questions.explain: The Integrated Portfolio performance must be a solo; ensemble playing is assessed in Component 04.

questions.q: What is the main educational purpose of pairing a performance with a composition in the portfolio?
options: To let learners develop and demonstrate skills as both performer and composer
To reduce the amount of listening study required
To replace the written examination entirely
To ensure every learner performs in a group
questions.explain: The integrated design encourages holistic development across performing and composing.

questions.q: A teacher marks a student's solo performance and own-brief composition, then OCR checks a sample of these marks. What is this checking process called?
options: Moderation
Invigilation
Appraising
Improvisation
questions.explain: OCR moderates the centre's marks for the non-examined Integrated Portfolio.

questions.q: Because the learner sets their own brief, in what style may the Component 03 composition be written?
options: Any style the learner chooses
Only Western classical style
Only the style of the OCR set works
Only popular music styles
questions.explain: The own brief allows composition in any genre or style the learner selects.

questions.q: A student is told the brief for their Integrated Portfolio composition will be provided by OCR. Why is this instruction incorrect?
options: In Component 03 the composition is to the learner's own brief; OCR-set briefs belong to Component 04
OCR never sets composition briefs for any component
All GCSE compositions must use an OCR brief
The Integrated Portfolio does not include a composition
questions.explain: The Integrated Portfolio composition is always to the learner's own brief, not an OCR-set one.

specSource: OCR GCSE (9–1) Music (J536) specification; Component: Integrated Portfolio
